transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi there, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. I, um, I hope I'm in the right place. They, uh, they sent me here from work. I'm an EMT, and I guess my lieutenant got a little worried about me. 

It's really nothing bad, I promise. I just... well, at the station, I was organizing the airway bags. I just wanted them to be in the right pattern, you know? It's important to be organized. And I might have been repeating some dispatch numbers out loud while I was doing it. Just to keep things straight in my head. 

My lieutenant told me to stop and step away, but... I just couldn't right then. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would just go bad. Does that make sense? I was just trying to keep everything safe, I hope you understand that. I wasn't trying to cause any trouble.

Can you tell me more about the thoughts you were having while organizing the airway bags? Were they thoughts that you didn’t really want to have, but they kept popping into your head, or did they feel more like something you needed to do to keep things safe?

Oh, no, it wasn't... it wasn't like thoughts I didn't want to have. Nothing bad like that, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think I'm having, you know, weird thoughts popping up out of nowhere. 

It was really just... I felt like I needed to do it to make sure everything was safe. Safety is just so important in my line of work, right? You always have to be prepared. I just felt like if the bags weren't in that exact pattern, and if I didn't say the numbers to sort of... lock it in, I guess... then something might go wrong on the next call. 

I really wasn't trying to be difficult or ignore my lieutenant when he told me to stop. I respect him a lot, and I'm usually a very good employee. I just wanted to be careful. I hope that doesn't sound too strange, Doctor. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
When you felt like you needed to finish organizing the airway bags and saying the numbers, did you feel anxious or upset if you thought you might not be able to finish it?

Well, I... I guess I did feel a little bit anxious, but not—not like a panic attack or anything extreme, I promise. It was more just a... a strong sense of responsibility, you know? 

When the lieutenant told me to stop, I just... I really couldn't step away. I know that sounds bad, like I was being insubordinate, but I swear I wasn't trying to be. It's just that I was moving the airway bags into this pattern that I knew was right, and I was saying the dispatch numbers, and... well, I felt like if I stopped, if I broke that sequence before it was done, the whole bay would just go bad. 

I just wanted everything to be perfectly set up so we'd be ready. I'd feel terrible if something happened because I didn't finish. I hope you can see I was just trying to do a good job, Doctor. I really didn't mean to cause a scene. Am I explaining that okay?
